title: Designing an Operant Behavior Modification Plan
description: Formulate a concrete behavioral intervention utilizing positive reinforcement, shaping, and schedule design.
problemStatement:
Design a 4-week operant conditioning plan to increase a productive behavior (e.g., daily 30-minute language study or regular exercise).

### Requirements:
1. Define the target operant behavior with a precise operational definition.
2. Establish an initial baseline measurement.
3. Choose an effective positive reinforcer and explain how you will prevent satiation.
4. Design a reinforcement schedule progression (e.g., starting with Continuous Reinforcement and fading to a Variable-Ratio or Fixed-Ratio schedule).
5. Explain why using positive reinforcement is superior to relying on positive punishment.
hints: Hint 1: Continuous reinforcement builds the habit quickly; partial schedules make it permanent.
Hint 2: Punishment often produces avoidance and anxiety rather than teaching the desired replacement behavior.
